Instead of focusing on all of the downfalls of religion (out-group hate), we should focus on how great atheism is (in-group love). So instead of been seen as a toxic community, we will be seen as a community that actually talks about atheism. That means that we should respect all other beliefs and respect their choice, not mock it. Not doing this is how /r/atheism got to be such a pretentious, hated community. We can do better.
I think we can all agree that we should do better than /r/atheism.

Why does it have to be one or the other? Why can't it be both? I agree with you that promoting atheism has a place, but criticizing religion is important too. When I think about my path to atheism, learning about what was wrong with religion was far more important than learning what was good about atheism.

I'd also suggest that we should not "respect all other beliefs" but instead respect the people who hold these other beliefs.

Maybe the easiest way to promote atheism is simply to be oneself as an atheist and show by example that it is quite possible to lead a normal and even potentially happy life without gods.
